title: Single-pair shortest path: simple-path enumeration vs Dijkstra
problem_statement: Given a directed graph on n vertices as an n x n matrix of arc weights in [0, inf] (an absent arc has weight math.inf; the diagonal is not used), s = 0 and t = n - 1, compute the minimum total weight of an s-t path (math.inf if there is none). The harness uses complete digraphs with weights 1..100.

input.size_measure: n^2 matrix entries (every input is a complete digraph whose absent arcs have weight inf).

algorithms.name: simple-path enumeration
algorithms.idea: Depth-first search over every simple path from s, recording the cheapest one that reaches t.
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n (n-2)!) on every n x n input: exactly 2P calls of the search with P = floor(e (n-2)!) (n >= 3), the number of simple s-t paths of the complete digraph, and n neighbour checks at each of the P calls not at t (PROOFS.md, section 2)
algorithms.correctness: With non-negative weights some shortest walk is a simple path, and all simple paths are enumerated (PROOFS.md, section 1).

algorithms.name: Dijkstra (array version)
algorithms.idea: Repeatedly settle the unsettled vertex with the smallest tentative distance and relax its out-edges.
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^2) with an array (linear in the n x n weight-matrix input; it reads exactly n(n-1)/2 distinct weights, for each pair of vertices the one leaving the vertex settled first), which is optimal up to a constant factor for weight-matrix input: for n >= 4 split the n - 2 vertices other than s, t into U (floor((n-2)/2) of them) and X, and set w(s, u) = 1, w(u, x) = 2 and w(x, t) = 1 for u in U, x in X, all other weights 100; then dist(s, t) = 4, and lowering any one weight w(u, x) to 1 makes it 3, so on this instance every correct deterministic algorithm (and every run of a zero-error randomized one, with its random bits fixed) reads all floor((n-2)^2/4) weights w(u, x), in the model where each step reads at most one entry and the steps depend only on the values read. PROOFS.md, sections 4 and 5. (Heap-based versions are background, not implemented.)
algorithms.correctness: Dijkstra 1959; proof in PROOFS.md, section 3: with non-negative weights, the minimum tentative distance is final when a vertex is settled.

relationship: Enumeration is factorial: Theta(n (n-2)!) = 2^Theta(n log n), super-exponential in the number n of vertices (2^Theta(sqrt(N) log N) in the N = n^2 matrix entries); Dijkstra's greedy settling order yields Theta(n^2).

background.statement: Dijkstra's algorithm with a Fibonacci heap runs in O(m + n log n) time for single-source shortest paths with non-negative weights (n vertices, m edges).

A deterministic O(m log^(2/3) n)-time algorithm computes single-source shortest paths in directed graphs with non-negative real weights in the comparison-addition model; its authors present it as the first to break the O(m + n log n) bound of Dijkstra's algorithm on sparse graphs.
background.source: Duan, Mao, Mao, Shu & Yin 2025, abstract

sources.note: Background only: the O(m + n log n) heap-based Dijkstra; not implemented.

sources.note: Background only: deterministic O(m log^(2/3) n) single-source shortest paths (see background); not implemented.

verification.method: V1: both agree on random complete digraphs with weights in [1, 100] (n <= 8 for enumeration); for n >= 2 harness.check only tests 0 < answer <= W[0][n-1] (for n = 1 it requires 0). V2: measured runtimes fitted against n (n-2)! and n^2 (timing data, not a proof). Proofs: PROOFS.md proves both implementations correct (also with absent arcs of weight inf), the enumeration's exact search-tree sizes on the complete digraph, Dijkstra's Theta(n^2) bound and the n(n-1)/2 weights it reads, the lower-bound instance and the space bounds; tests/test_proofs_sp.py checks them (72 digraphs against a Floyd-Warshall written in the test, plus Dijkstra for n = 9..30; search calls and weight reads for n = 2..9; Dijkstra's reads on 40 digraphs; the lower-bound instance for n = 4..12; recursion depth and tracemalloc peaks).

caveats: The enumeration's work depends only on n: its control flow never looks at the weights, and every input matrix is a complete digraph whose absent arcs have weight inf. A variant that skips absent arcs is not implemented and not claimed. Negative weights are outside the problem: both correctness arguments use non-negative weights.
notes: Possible further T3 steps (not entries of this dataset; their bounds are background): array Dijkstra Theta(n^2) -> Fibonacci-heap Dijkstra O(m + n log n) -> Duan et al. 2025 O(m log^(2/3) n) on sparse graphs.
